newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX JGBs, Euroyen ease back from record highs.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX JGBs, Euroyen ease back from record highs.

text.p: SIMEX Japanese government bond (JGB) futures eased off record territories late on Thursday after an early rally fuelled by arbitrage buying, dealers said.
After opening at its day low of 126.15, December JGBs spiked to a record high of 126.59 in early trade after a fixed interest arbitrade trade by a European trading house.
The trading house was said to have sold Nikkei futures and bought JGBs.
Dealers said healthy buying was seen at 126.20/58 for December JGBs. December JGBs ended 0.32 up at 126.20 on a turnover of 335 lots.
The surge in JGBs to new contract highs propelled Euroyen up in tandem, dealers said.
After hitting a high at 99.35, June Euroyen stayed range-bound at 99.33-99.34 for most part of the afternoon.
Dealers said Euroyen was underpinned by a market consensus that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) would maintain a steady rate policy and the BOJ's operations on Thursday reinforced this belief.
Dealers said Japan's October industrial production data, which showed a 3.5 percent growth in output from the previous month, failed to excite the market as it was within expections.
One dealer with a European institution said June Euroyen, at 99.33, had already priced in the BOJ's steady rate policy until next summer.
June Euroyen settled at 99.33 against its previous IMM close at 99.28. Turnover was 16,905 lots.
Eurodollars were lacklustre due to the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday.
June Eurodollars ended at 94.43, just one tick up from its previous IMM close on a meagre volume of 1700 lots.
